name: Lake Plateau and Sulu Arc
inspired_by: The southern Philippines as of 2026, compressed onto one map: a Lanao-type volcanic lake plateau with Maranao lakeside towns in the north-west, a Liguasan-type river marsh and jungle-covered cordillera in the centre, and a coconut coast facing a Sulu-type chain of volcanic islands with stilt villages over reef flats in the south. Small Islamic State-aligned cells (Dawlah Islamiyah factions and pro-IS Abu Sayyaf remnants, much reduced since the 2017 Marawi siege) still clash with the Armed Forces of the Philippines, which hold the towns and roads; the Bangsamoro autonomous region set up under the 2014 peace agreement governs the Muslim-majority areas. All towns are fictional.
climate: Tropical rainforest and monsoon (Koppen Af/Am) on the coast and marsh, 25-33 C all year with 2,000-3,500 mm of rain; the lake plateau at 700 m is cooler (18-28 C) and misty. Mindanao lies mostly south of the typhoon belt, but monsoon rains bring floods and landslides.
seasons: Amihan (Dec-Mar): north-east monsoon, drier, calmer seas in the island chain, clear mornings on the plateau
Hot dry spell (Apr-May): hottest, lowest marsh water, burning cogon grass
Habagat (Jun-Oct): south-west monsoon rains, flooded marsh and rice fields, rough seas, river crossings close
Transition (Nov): heavy showers, landslides on cordillera roads, harvest

vegetation: secondary growth with bamboo and climbing rattan
abaca and coffee patches in clearings
rice paddies and corn on the lake shore
coffee and fruit trees (lanzones, durian) around houses
reeds and water hyacinth at the lake edge
rice paddies on the marsh rim
beach morning glory and pandan on the strand
secondary forest on the volcanic cones
coral reef flats exposed at low tide

terrain.relief: A lake plateau at 650-750 m in the north-west, rimmed by volcanic cones to 1,200 m; a jungle-covered cordillera of steep ridges (600-1,650 m) across the centre; a marsh basin near sea level (5-20 m) in the east-centre; a narrow coastal plain in the south; and a chain of small volcanic islands (cones of 200-600 m) across a reef-studded strait.
features: crater lake plateau with a lake outlet river and falls
knife-edge jungle ridges and landslide scars
a river marsh with channels and floating vegetation
volcanic island cones with coconut slopes
reef flats with stilt villages and seaweed farms
limestone caves on the cordillera flank
terrain.water: A large plateau lake, its outlet river cutting a gorge to the sea, a slow river feeding the marsh (floods in the habagat), many streams, a strait with reefs, channels and tidal flats between the islands.

generator.approach: Heightmap at 10 m with bathymetry as negative heights. Plateau as a raised flat block with a lake basin stamped in; volcanic cones as radial stamps; the cordillera as ridged noise along a NW-SE axis; the marsh as a flattened low basin with a channel network; the island chain as cone stamps rising from a shallow shelf with reef masks at -0.5 to -3 m.

noise_layers.type: plateau step with lake basin stamp
noise_layers.purpose: north-west lake plateau and crater lake
volcanic cones on the plateau rim and the islands
reef and seagrass mask on the shelf; mangrove mask on tidal flats

generator.erosion: Strong hydraulic erosion on the cordillera for deep V-valleys and gullies; landslide scars as random slope stamps; deposition fans where streams leave the hills.
generator.rivers: Lake outlet river as a spline from the plateau through a gorge with falls to the sea; marsh river as a meandering spline with 8-15 side channels; streams by flow accumulation; the marsh water level and flooded area are a seasonal variable.
generator.settlement_flattening: Lakeside town flattened on the lake terraces; coastal towns on the plain behind the beach; hill barangays per plot on ridge shoulders; stilt villages need no flattening (posts into the reef flat).
generator.notes: One coastal highway and one plateau road are the only paved links; jungle trails, rivers and boats do the rest. The marsh and the island interiors are where cells hide; the habagat floods the marsh and grounds helicopters for days.

settlements.architecture: Maranao-type lakeside town: two- to four-storey concrete and cinder-block shophouses with steel shutters and tin or concrete roofs, painted signs, a large domed mosque with minarets, madrasas, a public market and a lake pier; a few carved okir-style wooden landmarks; one quarter left as a rebuilt zone with new concrete public buildings among cleared lots (inspired by post-2017 reconstruction).
settlements.wall_class: Reinforced concrete frames medium-thick; cinder-block infill thin (breachable); tin roofs no cover.
layout_rules: grid of streets around the market and the main mosque
lake promenade and pier with boats
municipal hall and police station on the plaza
army detachment at the town entrance

settlements.architecture: Barangay of wooden and bamboo houses on short stilts with tin or nipa roofs, a few concrete-block houses, a small mosque or chapel, a madrasa, a sari-sari store, a basketball court and a covered gym as the community hall.
settlements.wall_class: Wood, bamboo and nipa none; concrete-block houses thin.
layout_rules: strung along a road or river bank
mosque or chapel, school and basketball court as the centre
rice paddies or coconut groves around
hill barangays on ridge shoulders with steep trails

settlements.architecture: Sama- and Tausug-type stilt-water village over the reef flat: plank houses on wooden posts with tin and nipa roofs, linked by narrow plank walkways to a jetty and a mosque on stilts; boats moored under the houses; seaweed drying racks.
settlements.wall_class: Planks and nipa none; walkways collapse under explosions (hazard).
layout_rules: over the reef flat 100-500 m from the shore
walkway spine to the jetty and mosque

settlements.architecture: Coastal port town (poblacion): Spanish-era grid with a plaza, municipal hall and church or mosque, concrete commercial strip, ferry terminal and fish port, jeepney terminal, a hospital and a provincial capitol on a rise.
settlements.wall_class: Concrete medium; block thin; port warehouses steel thin.
layout_rules: ferry terminal and fish port on the waterfront
highway bypass with fuel stations and a checkpoint

settlements.architecture: Army brigade camps and detachments (sandbag and concrete bunkers, barracks, helipad, motor pool), police stations with blast walls, a coconut processing plant, a banana plantation packing house, a diesel power barge.
settlements.wall_class: Sandbag and concrete bunkers thick; barracks and sheds thin.
layout_rules: detachments on hilltops above villages and at bridges
brigade camp near the coastal town with helipad and pier

settlements.architecture: Coconut and rice farm hamlets: a wooden house on stilts, a copra dryer, a carabao shed, a small boat on the river.
layout_rules: on the marsh rim and coconut coast

infrastructure.roads: A two-lane coastal highway and a winding plateau road (landslide-prone in the rains) are the only paved routes; barangay roads of gravel, jungle trails on the ridges, river and sea routes everywhere else.
infrastructure.power: Grid power on the coast and plateau from a lake-outlet hydro plant (falls), diesel barges and generators on the islands; frequent outages.
infrastructure.ports: Ferry terminal and fish port at the coastal town; jetties and boat landings in every island village; a lake pier.
infrastructure.airfields: A short regional airstrip near the coastal town; army helipads at the brigade camp and detachments.
infrastructure.checkpoints: Army and police checkpoints on the highway, at bridges and at the plateau road entrance; Bangsamoro police posts in towns; coast guard and navy boardings in the strait.

pois.description: Hidden camp on a cordillera ridge: tarp shelters under the canopy, a cooking area, a lookout over the trail, a small explosives cache (map hazard) and a flag; reachable only on foot.
pois.contract_use: raid a cell camp; HVT capture (client phl)

pois.description: Stilt hut and boat landing deep in the marsh, reached by channel; reeds limit sight; booby-trap hazards marked.
pois.contract_use: boat-borne raid on a hideout (client phl)

pois.description: Hut cluster in an island's coconut uplands where kidnap victims are held; lookouts on the cone above the beach.
pois.contract_use: hostage rescue from the island chain (client phl)

pois.description: A lakeside quarter rebuilt after an earlier siege: new concrete public buildings, a rebuilt mosque, cleared lots and a few ruined shells; civilians returning.
pois.contract_use: VIP protection during a visit; counter-surveillance (client phl)

pois.description: Hilltop detachment with sandbag bunkers, a radio mast and a helipad above a barangay; targeted by harassment fire.
pois.contract_use: defend or relieve a detachment (client phl)

pois.description: Concrete bridge over the lake-outlet river with a checkpoint, a fuel station and roadside stalls.
pois.contract_use: route security; convoy escort chokepoint (client phl)

pois.description: Coastal-town ferry terminal and fish port: crowds, cargo, speedboats and outrigger bancas.
pois.contract_use: maritime interdiction of a cell's speedboat; VIP arrival (client phl)

pois.description: Reef-flat stilt village with plank walkways, a mosque on stilts and seaweed racks.
pois.contract_use: cordon and search with navy boats; evacuation in a storm (client phl)

pois.description: Concrete school used as a polling centre: classrooms, a covered court, a perimeter wall and a crowd on election day.
Cave in the cordillera flank used as a weapons cache; narrow entrance, chambers, a stream.
Banana or coconut packing plant with sheds, lorries and a workers' compound; extortion target.
pois.contract_use: protect workers from an extortion attack (client phl)

pois.description: Army brigade camp near the coast: barracks, motor pool, helipad, pier, adviser compound.
pois.contract_use: staging; briefing; adviser liaison (clients phl, usa)

weather.visibility_notes: Jungle canopy limits sight to 20-50 m; downpours cut visibility and ground helicopters; mist on the plateau and ridges in the morning; reed beds hide boats in the marsh.

civilians.behaviour: Busy markets and roads by day; fishermen out at dawn; Friday prayers fill mosques; jeepneys and motorbike taxis everywhere; families flee to the town or evacuation centres when fighting starts and return quickly. Clan feuds (rido) add armed civilians who are not a faction; carrying guns is common, so threat identification matters.
civilians.casualty_risk_notes: High density in towns, stilt villages and markets; armed civilians from clan feuds are a readable cue, not targets. The casualty rule bites in stilt-village and market contracts.

factions_present.where: Towns, highway and plateau-road checkpoints, hill detachments, the brigade camp; navy and coast guard boats in the strait; Marines on the islands.

East Asia cells (Dawlah Islamiyah-type and pro-IS Abu Sayyaf remnants): jungle camps on the cordillera, the marsh interior and the island uplands; speedboats between islands; extortion and kidnapping.
A small non-combat adviser team at the brigade camp and ISR drones overhead; never in front-line combat.

frontline: No front line: a cell hunt. Each isis-held zone (camp, hideout, island upland) raises a local threat level that posts extortion, kidnapping and IED events in nearby barangays. phl clear-and-hold operations (and player contracts for phl) flip a zone to cleared; cells regenerate in the marsh or the islands within weeks unless detachments are built. Election and Ramadan periods raise event rates; the habagat floods the marsh and freezes movement there. Clan-feud flare-ups are neutral events that block roads.
contract_hooks: Raid a cell camp on a jungle ridge and capture its leader (client phl)
Boat-borne raid on a marsh hideout (client phl)
Hostage rescue from an island upland (client phl)
Intercept a cell speedboat in the strait (client phl)
Election-day security at a polling centre (client phl)
Relieve a hill detachment under harassment fire (client phl)
Cache recovery from a limestone cave (client phl)
Escort an aid convoy on the plateau road after a landslide (client phl)
Adviser liaison and ISR-guided recon of a suspected camp (client usa)

hot_zones.name: Cordillera and marsh edge
hot_zones.layout: isis HQ in a ridge camp; 3-4 outposts (marsh hideout, cave cache, hill barangay safe house, river landing); phl detachments and highway checkpoints as friendly anchors; roaming cell pairs on trails and pump boats on channels; 1 QRF of cell fighters by boat

insertion.fob: LHD offshore in the strait for island and coastal contracts (amphibious landings with AAVs on beaches; boats over the reef flats); FOB at the army brigade camp near the coastal town for plateau and cordillera work. Helicopters in dry weather; on foot on ridges.

early_game_notes: isis (early tier) is the only hostile faction here and fights in small cells, which makes this a good early-game counter-terror map; phl (early, friendly client) and the US advisers give early clients. Captain-confirmed new theatre (2026-10-10).
